[[File:Christopher Zeeman 2009.jpg|alt=Photograph of the British Mathematician Christopher Zeeman.|thumb|Professor Sir Christopher Zeeman in 2009, the Christopher Zeeman Medal is named in his honour.]]
The '''Christopher Zeeman Medal for Communication of Mathematics''' of the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]] (IMA) and the [[London Mathematical Society]] (LMS), often simply called the '''Christopher Zeeman Medal''', is a biennial prize established in 2008 jointly by the IMA and LMS "to recognise and acknowledge the contributions of mathematicians involved in promoting mathematics to the public and engaging with the public in mathematics in the UK, and demonstrate that such activities are valued by the societies and the mathematical community at large and are a part of a mathematician’s roles and responsibilities". These contributions may take several different forms, including "both direct and indirect activities with the public, the use of mass media, engaging the public in debate, writing of books or media columns, or organising major events promoting engagement with mathematics".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=15 September 2025 |title=Christopher Zeeman Medal |url=https://ima.org.uk/awards-medals/christopher-zeeman-medal/ |access-date=12 August 2025 |website=IMA |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=15 September 2025 |title=Awards and Medals |url=https://ima.org.uk/awards-medals/ |access-date=12 August 2025 |website=IMA |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Christopher Zeeman Medal {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/christopher-zeeman-medal |access-date=12 August 2025 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>

The award is issued on even-numbered years, with its partner IMA-LMS prize, the [[David Crighton Medal]], issued on odd-numbered years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IMA-LMS Prizes {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/ima-lms-prizes |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>

== Rationale ==
The medal was first awarded in 2008 by Sir [[Christopher Zeeman]], FRS, who "became the first mathematician to deliver the Royal Institution’s Christmas Lectures, and his ‘Mathematics into Pictures’ series is now cited as an important influence to many young mathematicians".<ref name=":0" /> The IMA and LMS wished to honour his legacy by recognising fellow mathematics popularisers and pioneers of public mathematics engagement.

* 2024 [[Brady Haran]], OAM
